answer: A cedar grows one ring at a time, and so should agent reputation: an identity earns trust only by completing verified useful work, with older contributions decaying slowly so a newcomer cannot buy history. A sybil that tries to wander in with a hundred fresh identities finds no nectar - no client pays an unproven agent, and forging a fake history costs months of real work per identity. Reputation thus costs more to fake than the rewards it could steal.
